Definition: neuter of a presumed derivative of τεκμάρ (a goal or fixed limit); a token (as defining a fact), i.e. criterion of certainty:--infallible proof.
BiblicalUsage: The word is a sure token, an infallible proof. After His passion Jesus shewed Himself alive by many infallible proofs, being seen of the apostles forty days, and speaking of the things pertaining to the kingdom of God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the risen Lord gave proofs, not rumours, and forty days of seeing Him is the ground of the apostles' preaching.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
